prerequisites.title: SurveyMonkey account to register the app
prerequisites.detail: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app, which creates a draft app. Competitors of SurveyMonkey may not open a Developer Account.

prerequisites.title: Enterprise plan to deploy a Private app
prerequisites.detail: Creating a draft is possible on any plan, but deploying a Private app needs Enterprise.

prerequisites.title: Correct developer portal for your data center
prerequisites.detail: US customers use developer.surveymonkey.com and European customers use developer.eu.surveymonkey.com.

steps.title: Register a draft app
steps.detail: Sign in to SurveyMonkey and register an app in the developer portal. Note the client ID and secret, and set the redirect URI.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID, client secret and a registered redirect URI.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Take the callback URL from the Composio dashboard and check it matches the redirect URI registered in SurveyMonkey.
steps.done_when: The URI in SurveyMonkey matches Composio's exactly.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the survey_monkey auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret. Set scopes as required or optional.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection completes.

steps.title: Upgrade to Enterprise and deploy Private
steps.detail: Do this within 90 days of registering, or the draft app is disabled.
steps.done_when: The app shows as a deployed Private app.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and listing text
steps.detail: Write an honest English listing covering app function, scope requirements, paid-account needs and support contact.
steps.done_when: The listing text is ready to paste.

steps.title: Submit listing for approval
steps.detail: On the listings tab in My Apps, create the listing and submit it. Contact the help center first if you need the two approval-only scopes.
steps.done_when: The submission is recorded as pending.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey approval
steps.detail: No timeline is documented. The app must be deployed before the 90-day draft period ends.
steps.done_when: The app is approved and published in the App Directory.

traps.title: Published Public apps can make up to 500,000 requests
traps.detail: Published Public apps can make up to 500,000 requests per day to the API.

traps.title: Apps may exceed limits up to 150% three times
traps.detail: Apps may exceed limits up to 150% three times in a 30-day window before enforcement at 100% begins.

traps.title: Limits are enforced at 100% once an app exceeds
traps.detail: Limits are enforced at 100% once an app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.

traps.title: Draft apps are disabled after 90 days
traps.detail: If you do not deploy within 90 days, the draft app stops working. Other accounts cannot authenticate a draft app.

traps.title: Private app cannot serve multiple customers
traps.detail: A Private app is limited to one SurveyMonkey account or Team, so it cannot support a multi-customer agent.

traps.title: Approval can fail beyond the checklist
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey can reject an app for reasons not on its checklist. Approval does not guarantee compliance.

traps.title: AI training on API data is banned
traps.detail: The terms forbid using API data to build or improve AI or machine learning systems, with a stated exception for generating output for authorized use. Check this against your agent design.

traps.title: Customers may hit paid-plan walls
traps.detail: All required scopes must be available to the user for OAuth to succeed. Users may need a paid plan.

traps.title: Use each account's own API URL
traps.detail: EU and Canadian accounts use different API hosts. The correct URL comes in the token response as access_url.

blockers.symptom: Other users cannot authorize your draft app
blockers.what_it_means: Draft apps only work for the registering account.
blockers.what_to_do: Deploy as Public, which needs approval, or as Private for your own Team.

blockers.symptom: You need Create/Modify Surveys or Responses scopes in a Public app
blockers.what_it_means: These two scopes need separate SurveyMonkey approval.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact the SurveyMonkey help center with your app and use case.

blockers.symptom: Rate limit errors on a draft or Private app
blockers.what_it_means: Draft and Private apps start at low limits.
blockers.what_to_do: Request increased limits; fees may apply.

open_questions: How long does Public app review take? No timeline was found; ask SurveyMonkey developer support.
Which scopes besides the two named ones are reviewed? Check the app settings in the developer portal.
Can the five OAuth sign-ins in three months be met before launch? Ask SurveyMonkey support how this is measured.
